page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8369HB processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 2 virtual CPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz and includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes no local storage and has a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also demonstrate average throughput. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores ranking in the bottom 10%. This performance gap is also evident in memory bandwidth benchmarks, where both read and write operations on large blocks register in the lowest decile.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.hfg7.large is positioned as a general-purpose entry-level instance. It is best suited for lightweight workloads that rely on single-threaded execution rather than parallel processing, such as basic web serving, simple scripting, or small-scale utility tasks. Due to poor performance in database operations, Redis transactions, and multi-threaded compilation, it is not recommended for high-throughput database hosting or intensive development pipelines. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, it offers dedicated CPU resources at a low entry footprint, though resource-dense or memory-bound applications will face performance bottlenecks.
